In 2024, 47% ($1.5 billion) of U.S. Customs and Border Protection detentions of electronics were PV-related (Jacobo 2024a; Philip Shen 2025), representing 5–8 GW of imports, or 10%–18% of all modules imported into the United dc States. • Uncertainty over the timing of tariffs and AD/CVD: Countries and companies face changing duties and tariffs and may not know the final rates until years after product sales. Such factors continue to create uncertainty for U.S. PV developers while motivating U.S. component manufacturing. Federal incentives for domestic manufacturing, including the 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Tax Credit (hereafter referred to as the “45X MPTC”) and the Section 45 and Section 48 domestic content bonus credits (hereafter referred to as the “domestic content bonus credit”)—along with the long-term uncertainty of import price stability—explain the emergence of U.S. wafer and cell capacity in 2024 (Figure 6).7 In previous years, little or no U.S. PV ingot, wafer, or cell manufacturing existed, while U.S. polysilicon producers made limited sales to overseas PV ingot manufacturers.8 Wafer and cell manufacturing require substantial capital expenditure (CapEx) to achieve minimum effective scales ($500 million to $1.5 billion), long construction times (at least twice as long as for module assembly), and more extensive permitting and engineering complexities around chemical and other safety hazards that are not present for module assembly, which are manageable yet create public concern and heightened regulatory oversight. Up to around 15% of U.S. PV installations could be met by domestic cell suppliers by 2027, assuming all operating facilities and facilities under construction in Q2 2025 come online (see Section 2.4.2). In 2024, the single U.S. cell manufacturer could serve 2% of U.S. PV modules produced (PV Tech Research 2025). There were no shipments of domestic wafers in 2024, with facilities under construction expected to start producing in 2025 and fully ramp by 2027. In Q2 2025, domestic c-Si wafer manufacturing capacities under construction exceeded domestic c-Si cell manufacturing capacity operating or under construction. Market pricing, trade policies, and the stability of manufacturing and system-level incentives will play a role in future production.
